results.title: Writing Algorithms FAQ > Datasets
results.content:
## Is Morningstar fundamental data point-in-time, or does it include restatements?

LEAN loads all Morningstar data with the "As Original Reported" figures, so later corrections to a reported figure don't change the history. When a filing date is present, the data uses it. For older symbols without a filing date, the file date is approximated as 45 days after the as-of date.

results.title: Writing Algorithms > Universes > Equity > Morningstar Migration
results.content:
## Introduction

Morningstar retired the Global Equity Data Feeds that supplied the [US Fundamental Data](https://www.quantconnect.com/datasets/morning-star-us-fundamentals) dataset and replaced them with the Equity Data Feeds. QuantConnect rebuilt the entire history of the dataset from the new feeds. Backtests that ran on the old dataset can produce different results on the new dataset.

The old dataset remains on the master branch of LEAN until October 10, 2026. From October 10 through the end of October, the master branch uses the new dataset and the old dataset is available on a separate branch. To use the new dataset now, [change the LEAN engine branch](https://www.quantconnect.com/docs/v2/cloud-platform/projects/lean-engine-versions#02-Change-Branches) of your project. The old dataset will be fully deprecated for backtesting and live trading on October 31, 2026.

## Migration Atlas

The migration atlas compares every value in the old fundamental data with the new data. You can filter it by year, property, and company, and expand each property group to show its properties and period windows. Each row shows whether the values are identical, changed, reduced, lost, or new, and the measured reason for each change. To view the atlas in a separate tab, open the [QuantConnect Morningstar Fundamentals Migration Atlas](https://cdn.quantconnect.com/i/tu/qc_migration_atlas_v3.html).

## Reporting Dates

The old feeds dated the ratio, growth, per-share, and average properties at the end of the reporting period. The company filed the statement behind these values weeks later. In the new dataset, these properties take the filing date of the statement they come from. Most of their values now arrive later than before, by a median of 63 days.

Backtests and research on the old dataset could read these values before they were public. Live algorithms only receive the data that the vendor delivers each day, so they never received these values early. Strategies that rebalance soon after the end of a fiscal period now wait for the filing before they receive the new values.

## Coverage

The new dataset starts in January 1998, like the old one, and covers more US Equities. A larger dataset changes universe selection, even for companies whose values didn't change. For example, if you select the 500 companies with the largest dollar volume that have fundamental data, the selection now comes from a larger pool. Companies near the cut-off can drop out of your universe. The `has_fundamental_data` property works as before and returns `True` for more securities.

results.content:
## Get Historical Data

To get the historical data of all the fundamental properties over specific period of time, call the `history` method with a start `datetime` and an end `datetime`. To view the possible fundamental properties, see the `Fundamental` attributes in [Data Point Attributes](https://www.quantconnect.com/docs/v2/writing-algorithms/datasets/morningstar/us-fundamental-data#99-Data-Point-Attributes). The start and end times you provide to these methods are based in the [notebook time zone](https://www.quantconnect.com/docs/v2/research-environment/initialization#04-Set-Time-Zone).

```python
start_date = datetime(2021, 1, 1)
end_date = datetime(2021, 2, 1)

# DataFrame of all fundamental properties
single_fundamental_df = qb.history(Fundamental, symbols[0], start_date, end_date, flatten=True)
set_fundamental_df = qb.history(Fundamental, symbols, start_date, end_date, flatten=True)
all_fundamental_df = qb.history(Fundamental, qb.securities.keys(), start_date, end_date, flatten=True)
all_fundamentals_df = qb.history(Fundamentals, start_date, end_date, flatten=True)

# Fundamental objects
single_fundamental_history = qb.history[Fundamental](symbols[0], start_date, end_date)
set_fundamental_history = qb.history[Fundamental](symbols, start_date, end_date)
all_fundamental_history = qb.history[Fundamental](qb.securities.keys(), start_date, end_date)

# Fundamentals objects
all_fundamentals_history = qb.history[Fundamentals](qb.securities.keys(), start_date, end_date)
```

The preceding method returns the fundamental property values that are timestamped within the defined period of time.

results.title: Writing Algorithms > Securities > Asset Classes > US Equity > Corporate Fundamentals
results.content:
## Historical Data

To get historical fundamental data, call the `history` method. The return type depends on how you call the method.

```python
ibm = Symbol.create("IBM", SecurityType.EQUITY, Market.USA)

# DataFrame of fundamental data for a given asset
df_history = self.history(Fundamental, ibm, timedelta(30), flatten=True)

# Fundamental objects
fundamental_history = self.history[Fundamental](ibm, timedelta(30))

# Fundamentals objects for all US Equities (including delisted companies)
fundamentals_history = self.history[Fundamentals](timedelta(30))

# DataFrame of fundamental data for universe constituents
df_history = self.history(self._universe, 30, Resolution.DAILY, flatten=True)

# Series of fundamental data for universe constituents
series_history = self.history(self._universe, 30, Resolution.DAILY)
for (universe_symbol, time), fundamental in series_history.items():
    highest_market_cap = sorted(fundamental, key=lambda x: x.market_cap)[-5:]
```

For more information about historical fundamental data, see [Equity Fundamental Data](https://www.quantconnect.com/docs/v2/research-environment/datasets/equity-fundamental-data).

## Data Updates

The US Fundamental dataset only provides the originally-reported figures. If there was a mistake in reporting a figure, the data value isn't fixed later. In live trading, new fundamental data is available to your algorithms at approximately 6/7 AM Eastern Time (ET) each day. The majority of the corporate data update occurs once per month, but the financial ratios update daily. If there is no new data for a period of time, the previous data is filled forward.
